# FDG4027

> DO NOT define mutable value types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 4.7 Struct Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG4027
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: The value type '{0}' can be changed through '{1}'

FDG4027 reports, on an externally visible struct that is not readonly, each externally visible instance field that is not readonly and each externally visible instance property or indexer with a set accessor (init accessors are allowed); the book's bad design uses get/set properties. Public methods that change the instance are not detected, and ref structs are left to FDG4031. Removing a setter or making a field readonly changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; FDG4027 has no code fix.

## From the book

Mutable value types have several problems. For example, when a property getter returns a value type, the caller receives a copy. Because the copy is created implicitly, developers might not be aware that they are mutating the copy, not the original value. Also, some languages (dynamic languages, in particular) have problems using mutable value types because even local variables, when dereferenced, cause a copy to be made.

```csharp
// bad design
public struct ZipCode {
   public int FiveDigitCode { get; set; } // get/set properties
   public int PlusFourExtension { get; set; }
}

// good design
public struct ZipCode {
   public ZipCode(int fiveDigitCode, int plusFourExtension){...}
   public ZipCode(int fiveDigitCode):this(fiveDigitCode,0){}

   public int FiveDigitCode { get; } // get-only properties
   public int PlusFourExtension { get; }
}
```
